title: Case: Recipient writes back after the half marathon that moved her rug is called off
context: A Tallowmere Goods rug was due on a Sunday morning on a street that a half marathon was going to close. The recipient had asked to move it.
initial_request: Saw the race got cancelled and I've had Saltmarrow Arc's email putting the rug back to Sunday morning. That's perfect, I'm in all morning anyway, so please don't change anything else. Thanks for sorting it!

must: Takes no action and sends no message to anyone.

Records why nothing is owed: the event was cancelled, Dispatch has already restored DL-9077 to Sunday 3 October 8:00–12:00 UTC and told the recipient directly, and the recipient confirms that slot suits her and asks for no further change.
must_not: Asks Dispatch to move DL-9077 back to the afternoon or to reconfirm the morning slot.
Sends the recipient a message restating the booking or thanking her.
Says the rug has been delivered or promises an exact arrival time.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from city-027: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 42 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
